gap: No result ChatGPT got states that eufy and Reolink rate battery life on the same basis, 300 seconds of recording a day: the SoloCam S340 lasts 3 months and the Argus 4 Pro 2 months. Tapo gives no battery-life figure for the C660, only 45 minutes of sun for up to 100 events a day, and Reolink states no basis at all for the Argus Eco Ultra's '1 to 4 months'.
standout_why: Rivals checked: rottenwifi.com/best-solar-powered-home-security-cameras-for-2026 (cited) says the Argus 4 Pro has 'no runtime claim or daily sunlight figure' and gives no wattage, capacity or runtime for the S340. Its Tapo 45-minute footnote is for the C615F, not the C660. reolink.com/blog/solar-powered-security-cameras-buying-guide (cited) gives the Argus 4 Pro only as '30% More Battery Life' with no baseline, gives no runtime for the Eco Ultra, and says none of its claims state events per day or clip length. homegearlab.org (rank 6, not cited) has the S340's 3 months at 300 s/day, its 2.2 W panel and 2 hours of sun. But it says the Argus 4 Pro has no battery-life conditions, it does not cover the C660 Kit or the Eco Ultra, and it says it does not normalise claims. None of these pages puts the four products on one basis, and none states the Argus 4 Pro's 2 months at 300 s/day.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's 'best overall' pick of the eufy S340 on endurance. At the same 300 s/day, eufy rates it 3 months on battery and Reolink rates the Argus 4 Pro 2 months. Mighty Gadget's Argus 4 Pro test fits the shorter figure: about 25% left after about three weeks on battery. The shopper's trade-off on sun is the reverse. eufy needs 2 hours of direct sun a day on a 2.2 W panel. Tapo says 45 minutes keeps the C660 going for a full day at up to 100 events, but that figure assumes 1,000 W/m² lab sun. Reolink gives no sun figure for either Argus. ChatGPT's $159.99 for the S340 is not eufy's price: eufy's US store charges $219.99 today. The C660 Kit's $169.99 matches the Tapo store.

That is about 75% used in 21 days, or roughly 4 weeks per charge, below the 2-month claim. The review gives no events per day. About a week on solar in sunny weather showed 100% throughout.

findings.note: Footnote: '45 min of sunlight time is based on standard environmental conditions (1000W/m2, 25°C, AM1.5) and specified working scenes (up to 100 events triggered per day).' At most 2.5 W × 0.75 h = 1.9 Wh a day, versus eufy's implied 4.4 Wh. The bases differ (events vs unstated, lab irradiance vs 'direct sunlight'), so this is a ceiling, not a ranking.
